title: No support for multilingual documentation tools (lp:#1354486)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1354486) created by **Marco Ciampa (ciampix)**
```
In KiCad EDA there is no support for multilingual documentation tools.
Documentation is written directly with OpenOffice, a simple Wordprocessor,
that does not handle automatic multilingual / multiformat document handling
like many OpenSource projects already do nowadays. See the GIMP for
example.

The problem.
Master documentation is written in OO. Suppose that some volunteer (like
me) is avid to translate it into a foreign language. Suppose that starting
from a specific version copy, working night and day, in a fiew months he
(me) is able to complete it. It wold be already obsolete because of the
improvement and new functions applied meanwhile in the master developmente
branch. Documentation, if you want to be ready when the development version
become stable, must be translated along with the development process.
Suppose you want to update. You (me) have to read all the master copy along
with the translated copy do see where the document is changed and how. This
work is many times more the translation effort in itself. If the situation
do not change this could be a very discouraging factor for translators.

The solution.
The aforementioned GIMP translation team use xml2po to face up to this
problem, another (better) tool is Publican
(https://jfearn.fedorapeople.org/en-
US/Publican/4.0/html/Users_Guide/index.html) but I think that there are
many more different tools out there.

A transition to the XML format will have the (benign) side effect to enable
context sensitive help, as is in GIMP, much appreciated by the users.
```

title: DRC and netclasses : clearance rules between nets of different potential (lp:#983230)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/983230) created by **Vesa Solonen (vesa-solonen)**
```
Flexible automatic design rules would need "differential net classes" that
means different rules for a net depending on surrounding nets.

As an example I'll explain the problem of a traditional power electronics
half bridge circuit:

HV----            [400V     10A]
     |
Gh--|<            [0-415V    1A]        [0 < V(Gh)-V(Sh) < 15]
     |
Sh-------> Out    [0-400V   10A]
     |
Gl--|<            [0-15V     1A]
     |
GND------>        [0V       10A]

HV net needs "power" class clearance and width towards all nets as does
Out. Sh needs "power" class clearance towards all nets, but Gh and width
according to "control" class. Gh needs the same, but "control" clearance
towards Sh. Gl needs "control" class clearance and width.

Curently this system is unrealisable using KiCad DRC. I propose adding a
"potential class" description to net class design rules to address this
problem. Needed data stuctures for file format support and implementation
need to be discussed and designed. Interested parties are encouraged to
comment here and aim for a production ready blueprint.
```

title: No support for technology files in PCBnew (lp:#961533)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/961533) created by **Andrew Zonenberg (azonenberg)**
```
Many other EDA tools allow a "technology file" to be created containing
standardized design rules for a specific fab process which can be imported
into a project rather than being typed in one at a time in a slow and
error-prone fashion. As far as I can tell kicad does not support anything
of the sort.

Basic workflow:
* Create PCBnew file and configure design rules
* File | Export technology file, specify file name
* Create new PCBnew file for a future project
* File | Import technology file, choose file name

The specific things that should be included in a tech file are:
* Global minimum trace size / spacing design rules
* Minimum via size design rules
* Soldermask clearance
* List of predefined trace and via sizes

This doesn't look like it'll be too hard to implement and I intend to
submit a patch in a week or two with a first-draft implementation.
```

```
System : scientific linux 6.0, X86_64
KiCAD version : (1) Pre-build rpm from EPEL, 2011-01-28 BZR 2765 stable
                          (2) 2011-0708 BZR-3044 -stable, build from source
code

Both version generate same wrong result.

While system use multi-voltage for digital component, annotate and netlist
writer generate
wrong result, the ERC will failure and wrong netlist generated.

How to re-produce:
      (1) open eeschema with a new design.
      (2) make Show Hidden Pin ON to see hidden power pin
      (3) place two 7404 gate from 74xx library,
      (4) 7404 gate 1, vcc connect to Power A (+5V, for example)
      (5) 7404 gate 2, vcc connect to Power B (+3.3V for example)
      (6) make annotate, 7404 gate 1 & 7404 gate 2 gets same U1
      (7) run ERC(with default option) got "Conflict problem bewteen pins
(power)"
      (8) Annotate error, because two 7404 gate from different power should
generate U1 & U2 , not only U1
      (9) So, the netlist will be wrong, beacause two different power
source connected togeger, and only one power net shows on netlist file.
      (10) if on step 6, we manual annotate 7404 gate 1 as U1, 7404 gate 2
as U2, run ERC and netlist also wrong

When use KiCAD to design signle-power system, everything works fine, but
when we design a multi-voltage system, the eeschema generate wrong netlist.

Both error (annotate & netlist writer) should be same bug in eeschema, and
should be modify with following:

When Annotate:
   (1) if hidden power pin manual connected to other net then go step 2,
else original eeschema work
   (2) checked power pin connected net name, same net name will be same
device else was different device

When Write Netlist:
   (1) if hidden power pin manual connected to other net name (+5V, for
examples), then net name change to the name connected not the original
name.

Work Around:
   Currently, we create ourself library for multi-voltage design, for
examples : 74XX with power name VCC, 74XX_3V3 with power name 3V3 .
```

title: wishlist: snap to object (lp:#806260)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/806260) created by **Berwyn Hoyt (berwyn)**
```
I'm an ex-user of Circad.  It has a super function called 'snap-to'.  Very
simply, it is a hotkey that moves the cursor to the centre of the nearest
object, whether that be a track end, a component pad, a line end, or
whatever.

Once you press the hotkey, the mouse cannot move the cursor for 2 seconds.
This gives you enough time to place whatever you want to place at that
point.

This feature also provides an easy way to place something to be an exact
space away from something else using the keyboard.  So if you want two
tracks spearated by exactly 2mm, then you snap to one end of the first
track, then use your keyboard to move the cursor exactly 2mm to the right
and hotkey-place the second track.  Very accurate and easy.  (Mind you,
Circad also had a nice feature which let you move 10x and 100x grid spacing
with the cursor keys by pressing Shift & Ctrl while arrowing -- that was
handy, too).

An example of when this snap-to is needed.  Trying to place a 2:1 rectangle
on the PCB_Edges layer.  I can start in top left corner, place a line to
the bottom, then a line to the right, then back up to the top, but how do I
know how far up to the top to go so that I'll meet the original starting
point exactly?  Use snap-to.
```

title: Add a warning for case sensitive differences (lp:#1843415)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1843415) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
If you name two hierarchical sheets with (very) similar names, like
"file1.sch" and "File1.sch", this will work on case sensitive file systems,
while it can generate errors in case insensitive file systems.

Although using filenames as such (mostly identical names for different
sheets) is not a good practice, it is still "legal" in eeschema, and
copying the project from a case-sensitive machine (i.e. Linux) to a case-
insensitive machine (i.e. dos/win) will lead to differences in the
behaviour.
For instance, if the two names refer to one child sheet and its parent this
will create a circular dependency on schematics and likely crash eeschema
on windows machines but not on Linux machines.

Cheers,
Dino.
```

title: eeschema - 'symbol fields'-editor  - linebreak in a component field makes schematic unreadable  (lp:#1842943)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1842943) created by **Otto Mikkonen (ottomaani138)**
```
When working with the new 'symbol fields'-editor in eeschema, I've
experienced a breakage of the associated .sch-file due to linebreaks
appearing on one of the component-fields.

I'm not exactly sure from where these linebreaks appear, but they somehow
make their way into the fields when copying component field-data from one
part to another. Somehow selecting a field graphically and copy-pasting it
to another sometimes selects a hidden linebreak, which then partially
breaks the associated .sch file. Could also be, that the linebreak
originates from an external source, like the part# from mouser.com.

Anyways, since these linebreaks can be so disastrous, I thought some added
resilience to how fields are managed would be neat. I.e., when linebreak is
encountered on a component field, it could be filtered out before saving
the .sch or something. I can't imagine a case, when linebreak is actually
wanted on a component field.

I added a screenshot on how the error-messages might look like when trying
to open up a broken schematic.
```

```
The documentation on building could be improved:

a) Excluding various build targets: The documentation states the flag, e.g.
"KICAD_SPICE" which can be used to exclude (or include) something, but
doesn't show, how (e.g. "To specifically override any of the build targets,
set the specific flag by adding '-D<YourFlag>=<Value>', e.g.
"-DKICAD_SPICE=0" in the cmake line below"

b) Default to more than a single-core build:
The build instruction says to use "make", which defaults to a single-core
build. Shouldn't that be "make -j <NumberOfCpuCores>"? Or at least a
recommendation that it can be used or why it shouldn't (if there is a
reason, not to)

c) USE_CCACHE: I know this from using android, which is why I explicitely
searched for it, and it indeed exists. A description of it and a default
usage (not by setting the flag, but by defaulting the build instructions to
using it) would be nice, imo

d) Exact packages: Most homepages for the additionally required packages
allow downloading windows binaries and source code for linux. I don't want
to source-build everything, there are prebuilts, so it would be nice to get
list of actual linux packages to install, e.g. "libglew-dev" for GLEW etc.

These have all occured to me while trying to set up and getting a build.
I hope this is still the right place for it. I didn't want to do a single
report for each of these, as they are targetting the same thing, hope this
is OK.
```

title: Schematic junction implementation (lp:#1842438)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1842438) created by **eelik (eelik)**
```
The next is copied from https://bugs.launchpad.net/kicad/+bug/1842355.

I'm not sure if this is the right place to talk about this, but I find the
concept of independent junction dot weird. Junction should be a property of
two or more wires crossing (or endpoints touching, or endpoint touching
another line) and there shouldn't exist any junction without two wire
lines.

From the standpoint of implementation it may be easier to have separate
junctions but they should very strictly depend on existence of a wire
crossing. For example, instead of

junction: xcoord,ycoord

there could be

junction:
   wire: id
   wire: id

But at least, if they are separate independent entities, they should be
updated very stricly with any change made to wires. The update mechanism
should be "waterproof". I've seen different situations when junction don't
correctly reflect changes made to the wires.

It shouldn't be possible to add junctions where there are no wires
crossing, and there should never be need to remove junctions except from
where wires are crossing. "Add junction" shouldn't blindly add a junction
dot, it should only make a junction out of two wires crossing each other.
```

title: Idea: compatibility section in file formats (contains warning texts to be printed when opened in older versions) (lp:#1842285)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1842285) created by **Rene Poeschl (poeschlr)**
```
I just discovered a possibly useful feature in the eagle file format. They
include a section called compatibility which contains warnings to be
printed if opened in an older version.

Might be something interesting to add to kicad to prepare for a time when
the file format becomes much more stable than it is now (If only minor
additions are made then these can possibly ignored by the user. But the
user would need to know what they loose by opening in an older version.
This is one way of telling an older version which warning messages to print
without the older version even being aware of the features it does not
support.)

It could theoretically also include information for the parser on how to
replace some unknown things such that they can parse the file kind of
safely.

For example it could contain information which file format tags can be
ignored without changing the outputed file. The differential net clearance
setting added with v5 would be such an example. Ignoring it does not change
the viewed file it only removes a routing feature.

Chamfered pads are a different beast. They would only be able to be
replaced by another similar pad type and therefore change the file ->
should be an error. But instead of a parser error it would then say "you
use a kicad version that does not understand chamfered pads introduced in
version 6.0.0." which is much easier to understand by the user. (in reality
a warning could then only be produced by 7.x features as 5.x and earlier
does not understand this feature. But i have no example for such a future
release.)
```

title: wishlist: eeschema: don't un-annotate on cut-and-paste (lp:#1842275)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1842275) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
In the current master version, when you cut and paste a part of a
schematic, it is un-annotated. On copy-paste that is good since you are
always adding components, but in a cut-paste it may let you loose some of
the work done.

Example:
You have a fully routed (complex) board.
You need to re-organize schematics moving some components from one sheet to
another, so you use "cut and paste" to do this.
When you paste the components they get un-annotated
When you re-synchronize the pcb you need to re-annotate components, then
the components you moved/reannotated are removed and put back as "new"
components with new reference, loosing the previous placement, so you need
to place the components once again. Also if the components get the same
reference they are removed and re-inserted as new components when you re-
syncronize the pcb.



Cheers,
Dino.

Note: may be this wish is related to Bug #1827503 "Implement more (and
custom?) annotation schemes"
```

title: Timestamp generation unsafe for scripting, year 2038 (lp:#1842253)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1842253) created by **Simon Richter (sjr)**
```
Looking at GetNewTimeStamp() in the aptly named common/common.cpp, this
takes the lower 32 bits (as that is the definition of timestamp_t) of
current Unix time and, if needed, increments it to avoid collisions when
multiple components are created in the same second:

    timestamp_t GetNewTimeStamp()
    {
        static timestamp_t oldTimeStamp;
        timestamp_t newTimeStamp;
        newTimeStamp = time( NULL );
        if( newTimeStamp <= oldTimeStamp )
            newTimeStamp = oldTimeStamp + 1;
        oldTimeStamp = newTimeStamp;
        return newTimeStamp;
    }

This is reasonably safe for GUI operation, as we can assume that it is
unlikely that the user creates a large number of components, then closes
and reopens the program, and proceeds to add more components.

When eeschema gains scripting support, this might fall flat though when one
script creates a large array of components and subsequently terminates (so
the record of the highest ID in use is lost), and the user then starts
another script or begins editing manually.

This will also break down in 2038, when the 32-bit counter wraps around.
This is less of a collision risk, but we lose ordering.

Two changes, both somewhat beginner friendly:

 - find out why we're limited to 32 bits and what needs to be done to
change this.

It should be safe to replace timestamp_t by time_t, but there was probably
a good reason why that wasn't done. This needs some archaeology.

 - Move oldTimeStamp into the SCH_SHEET class and update it during load.

This requires that everyone generating timestamps does so with a sheet as
context, and there might need to be some handling for duplicate timestamps
on different sheets.

It might also make sense to stop generating identifiers from the current
time and just use incrementing numbers -- but we need to get better at
detecting duplicates then.
```

title: Board print out for identical components for assembly purposes (lp:#1841945)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1841945) created by **Art (diametrix)**
```
When I do a manual assembly of a prototype, I usually have to use different
color markers for multiple identical footprints (components) to speed up
the assembly.  It is especially useful if assembling multiple prototypes.

For example, if I have five identical 10K resistors in the schematic I will
highlight them with the same color in the board printout and in the BOM, so
I can populate them all at the same time.  The problem is - it takes time
and eventually you run out of colors.  It would be a neat feature if you
could automatically print a board layout with identical components printed
in bold and the rest of the board greyed out all on separate sheets.

For example, when I print a board layout for the assembly purposes I print
only silkscreen, paste, Fob and mask layers for each side of the board.
Let's say you have a check box in the print dialog to collate sheets based
on the components.  When checked, instead of one page print you will get as
many pages as there are unique components on the board, with each page
containing all the layers I selected to be printed and only the current set
of components printed in bold and the rest of the board greyed out (still
visible but barely)
```

```
need familiarity with the KiCad codebase.

reported for the 3D viewer, where data types are different between
translation units that are later linked. This doesn't seem to have adverse
effects, as these different definitions seem to be compatible, but it is
still an indication that something is not entirely correct.

Since GLM has some compile time options configured through preprocessor
macros, my expectation is that the macros it is sensitive to are not
consistent around all uses of the GLM library. The warning messages
themselves point to different implementations of the glm::vec3 type being
used:

SMATERIAL' violates the C++ One Definition Rule [-Wodr]
 } SMATERIAL;
   ^
/var/lib/jenkins/workspace/linux-kicad-head-
lto/src/include/plugins/3dapi/c3dmodel.h:57:3: note: a different type is
defined in another translation unit
 } SMATERIAL;
   ^
/var/lib/jenkins/workspace/linux-kicad-head-
lto/src/include/plugins/3dapi/c3dmodel.h:39:13: note: the first difference

/var/lib/jenkins/workspace/linux-kicad-head-
lto/src/include/plugins/3dapi/c3dmodel.h:39:13: note: a field of same name

lto/src/include/plugins/3dapi/xv3d_types.h:47:25: note: type 'struct
```

title: wishlist: eeschema block select for hierarchical sheet pins (lp:#1841555)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1841555) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Problem: selecting a lot of hierarchical sheet pins can be time consuming,
since the block selection on hierarchical sheet pins seems not implemented
(or does not work).

Using shift+leftclick or ctrl+leftclick works, but needs to select the pins
one-by-one and can be tedious when you modified the schematic and you have
to delete or move a lot of pins.
In current version CTRL+click and SHIFT+click act the same way on sheet pin
selection.

Wish 1:
Enable the block selection on hierarchical sheet pins.

Wish 2:
Have shift and ctrl work as in "list" selection: clicking on a pin item and
shift-clicking on another would select all the pins between them on the
border of the hierarchical child sheet.  The default behaviour could be
"clockwise", so changing the order of the selected two mostly inverts the
selection.

Any of the two wishes solves the problem.

P.S.: ctrl-clicking on an item behaviour is good as it is now.

Possible problems: without a selection filter to choose if you want to
select or not hierarchical sheet pins, block selection could lead to
"strange" behaviours, for instance when you want to "block select" a part
of the schematics and get a multiple selection of components, wires and
some hierarchical sheet pins.

Cheers,
Dino.
```

title: group buses incorrectly handle braces  (lp:#1840834)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1840834) created by **Brendan Haines (brendanhaines)**
```
When using {braces} notation of buses, the first name gets messed up by the
open brace.

BUSNAME{A B C}
should mean a bus with 3 members: "A", "B", and "C"
it instead is interpreted as having members: "brace}A", "B", and "C"

This incorrect interpretation is applied as follows:
Labels and hierarchical ports add "brace}" invisibly as above.
Hierarchical sheet pins act differently. Using the "import hierarchical
sheet pin" automatically inserts "brace}" which (unlike labels/ports) can
be seen and removed by editing the pin but does not appear in the text in
the schematic.

My current workaround is to add an extra bus member "A" to the beginning of
every bus and add "brace}" to every hierarchical sheet pin.

To connect using a bus from within one hierarchical sheet to another
requires the following names:
wire BUSNAME.B
bus BUSNAME{A B}
hierarchical label BUSNAME{A B}
hierarchical sheet pin BUSNAME{brace}A B}        << Note this is different
bus BUSNAME{A B}
wire BUSNAME.B


I will follow up with some pictures.
```

title: Eeschema has Save and Save All (lp:#1840383)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1840383) created by **Seth Hillbrand (sethh)**
```
The horizontal toolbar is tied to "Save All" while the Hotkey is set to
"Save"

While we do use a document-based file format, I don't think that there's a
good usecase for differentiating between "Save" and "Save All".  In a
multi-document interface, you might have multiple, /independent/ documents
open at once, so having two kinds of Save makes sense.

Eeschema can never have multiple independent sheets open.  They can only be
hierarchically linked, so allowing one sheet to be saved but another to not
be invites more trouble than it is meant to avoid.
```

title: Implement support for STEP compression (lp:#1839893)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1839893) created by **Harvie (harvie)**
```
packages3d directory takes 5GB of my diskspace, while i've installed it
from ~300MB archlinux package. Can you please add support for compression?
There are compressed versions of both VRLM and STEP, using extensions
.wrl.gz and .stpZ, both supported by FreeCAD.

I think it would make sense to support this. Maybe you can simplify and
just use .wrl.gz and .step.gz.

I suggest to implement this in such way, that user will enter path to
uncompressed model (without ".gz") and if there's no such file, kicad can
take a second look to version with ".gz" suffix. So it will be possible to
compress whole library without having to change existing PCB files or
limiting ability to modify the models without having to recompress them
every time.

BTW why library contains all models in two formats? Can't we just stick to
one of them? I guess that STEP is more modern, but VRLM takes 4 times less
space.
```

title: eeschema cut and paste annotation lost (lp:#1839348)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1839348) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Cutting a part of a schematic to paste it somewhere else looses components
annotation.

To reproduce:
  Select a component
  cut it with ctrl-x or right-click-menu->cut
  paste it with ctrl-V or right-click-menu->paste.
  The component annotation of the pasted items is lost.

This can be a problem when on complex projects you have to re-organize
schematics but you have yet routed the board: re-annotating the components
generates a schematic that is not in-sync with the pcb and re-syncronizing
it (F8) with different annotation may be is not so easy (did not try it: I
have a too complex board).


In "copy-paste"operation is correct to clear components annotation, since
without doing that we would end up to a "duplicate references", but in
"cut-paste" the annotation should be kept.

May be the easiest way to handle this correctly is:
 -after a cut or copy the reference of the components in clipboard should
be reset only if that reference exist in the project (this handles also the
case where cut is followed by more than one paste)
Since a copy does not remove the components the cut-paste, copy-paste, cut-
paste-paste-paste, copy-paste-paste-paste... are all handled the same way.

On the 5.1.2 version the cut+paste works correctly without loosing
annotation.
On the 5.1.4 version the cut+paste works correctly without loosing
annotation.

May be this issue is related to the fix for Bug #1833205 (I did not verify
if it is true, but that one also is about component annotation in copy-
paste operations)

Cheers,
Dino.
-----------------------------------
```

```
weakens the "pin not connected" check. I would suggest to add additional
checks for this.

error)
```

title: wishlist: tool options on tool button right click (lp:#1839245)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1839245) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Preface:
Now to set a tool option in pcbnew you have to select the tool and use the
popup menu, find the item and set the correct options (as an example I'm
thinking about the routing options).
In programs like GIMP to set a tool option you double-click the tool
button.

Wish: add the tool button double-click action to set tool parameters.

A list of parameters that could be set in such a way is:

Selection tool: Set a selection filter (object based, not yet implemented
but in wishlist #1793216 and coming in kicad 6)
Show ratsnest: select curved/straight line for ratsnest
Push-n-shove router: open "interactive router settings" dialog
Line/circle/arc: Set default line parameters (not the layer that will be
the current layer)
Dimension: Line width, text width-height... (not the layer that will be the
current layer)

DRC button: Open board setup->DRC rules

Of course this is a minimal list and there will be a lot of things I did
not think about.

For eeschema the same could be done, for instance on the graphic line/text
toolbuttons to set default color/size etc.

The advantages of this method are that it is more intuitive than the
shortcuts (to use them you have to learn them), and faster than searching
the correct sub-menu.


Cheers,
Dino.
```

title: CAM output automation / CAM manager combining all plotting and manufacturer data creation (lp:#1838987)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838987) created by **Rene Poeschl (poeschlr)**
```
From https://bugs.launchpad.net/kicad/+bug/1808013/comments/2 (It was
suggested to spawn a wishlist bug as the reported problem has been fixed.)

---

Long-term suggestion: Get rid of the current plot dialog and create a new
CAM output dialog combining gerber generation, drill file generation and
position file generation. (And possibly also some other things)

It is quite confusing right now. If i want to create gerber why would i not
want the drill file to be created. Yes i will want to have the same
settings available as with the drill dialog right now but some of them
should only be setable in one place. One example would be the use of the
auxilary origin. If it is enabled in gerber then i will want it in the
drill and position file as well.

Some of the current plot features could be either export or print options
(export to svg instead of plot to svg. Print to pdf instead of plot pdf.)
Or we could decide that they are simply other datatypes for the CAM export.

Such a CAM dialog could then also handle exporting and importing CAM
settings. And handle future more powerful data types (successors for
gerber)
```

[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838708) created by **Dan Green (danngreen)**
```
Copy/paste in eeschema is great, but I found it sometimes gets mixed up
when I'm copying text (like library:symbol name) and instead gets a
component data ($Comp... etc.) on the clipboard.

I think I narrowed it down to the Symbol chooser window changing the source
of Copy when using the main menu bar (but not the contextual pop-up menu).

To replicate (tested only on OSX):

1) Open any schematic
2) Open the Symbol Properties window for any symbol
3) Click the icon for "Browse Library" which opens the Choose Symbol window
4) Close the Choose Symbol window by clicking Cancel
5) Select the text in any text box in the Symbol Properties window.
6) Select "Copy" from the main Edit menu, or press Cmd+C (if you right-
click or control-click and select Copy from the context menu, the bug will
not appear)
7) Press Cmd+V to Paste: the entire symbol will be pasted into the
schematic window (rather than the text you selected being pasted into the
text box). Or, go over to your favorite text editor and hit Paste: you'll
see $Comp...$EndComp is in the clipboard instead of the text you had
selected when doing the Copy.
```

title: Misleading "Update footprints" text in "Update PCB from Schematic" (lp:#1838551)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838551) created by **eelik (eelik)**
```
The "Update PCB from Schematic" dialog - opened from eeschema or pcbnew -
has an option "Update footprints". The UI text is misleading. I have seen
at least two threads in the user forum where a poster was confused by that,
trying to update footprint(s) on a board after modifying the footprint
module files.

The confusion comes from using the word "update" in two completely
different contexts with footprints. What the "Update PCB from Schematic"
dialog actually does is change (or not) the footprints if the footprint
associations, i.e. footprint names, have been changed in symbols of the
schematic. I think the UI text should reflect that. The word "update"
should in my opinion be reserved for updating from the changed library
file.

I would even go as far as to say that the dialog UI text could be "Don't
change footprints" or "Keep old symbol/footprint associations" or something
like that, and the default would be not selected.

In the minimum it should have a tooltip text which explains what it does.
Now none of the Options has a tooltip.
```

description:

```
the link to "Edit pre-defined sizes". IMHO This was a nice feature.  Thanks
for doing it.

Now I suggest that other similar functions have links to configuration
setting pages. This is a bit of a philosophical design change, but has the
potential to provide a more friendly user experience.

CONVENIENT to have a button there to jump to the page (popup, whatever)
that configures the Rules. This may require multiple buttons depending on
the number of setup parameter locations.

idea), but rather an assist to both noobs and experienced users alike.

Sorry I'm not a dev, but I'd be happy to help if I can.

Barry
```

title: track current capability analysis (lp:#1838171)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838171) created by **Oleg Endo (oleg.endo)**
```
When designing power distribution stuff, it's of course important to get an
overview of current capability of the traces.  We've got the pcb calculator
which is a nice supplementary tool to get some estimates.  However,
analysis of actual layout requires more work and has to be done manually.

It'd be really useful if there was a way to analyze a net and/or a
subsection/area of a net for current carrying capability.  Perhaps it's
difficult to get a perfect detailed analysis, but a rough estimate would
already be really helpful and speed up the design process.  Most of the
info is already available:
  - copper layer thickness
  - inner layers vs. outer layers
  - stitching via sizes (can use rough estimate for via current)

The max. desired temperature rise variable could be stored as a board
settings option or somehow entered in the UI for the analysis.
```

description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838140) created by **Diego Herranz (diegoherranz)**
```
Hi, all.

I'm using nightlies and facing a weird bug with buses. I was wondering
whether it can be related to recent bus upgrades.

I've got a bus:
ROW0, ROW1, ROW2, ROW3, ROW4, ROW5, ROW6, ROW7, which on the PCB layout
becomes
ROW0, ROW0, ROW0, ROW0, ROW0, ROW0, ROW0, ROW7 ???
It seems to be semi-random and I've seen other combinations too.

I've managed to reduce the SCH to a minimal example (attached). Further
changes to this seem to fix it somehow, so I couldn't reduce it anymore.
Note that one of the symbols is not on the official library so I've
included a local library.
I've tried replacing that symbol for a standard header, but that seems to
fix the problem, although I can't see anything wrong with the symbol
itself.

I asked on the development mailing list and jp charras confirmed it:

> I confirm there is a serious issue shown by this sample: the netlist is
broken.
> Moreover, when I try to add a bus name ("ROW[0..7]") to the bus, Eeschema
crashes.
> Looks like the bug has something to do with hierarchical labels.

> I do not see issues with the schematic.

I agree it is a serious one too given it breaks the netlist. I've got a SCH
which I can't layout because of this. It's not an important project and
that is why I'm using nightlies, but now I can't open the layout on 5.x
stable because the format changed :)

Many thanks!
```

description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1838021) created by **Art (diametrix)**
```
If I try to find a symbol in an existing schematic and type it's name in
the Find text box, that symbol reference field becomes highlighted but the
cursor doesn't move to the symbol.  That doesn't help me at all if the
symbol is off the screen or more frequently under the Find pop-up window.
Now if I hit the Find button I get the message about reaching the end of
the schematic and nothing being found.  Only if I hit Find button again
will it actually move the cursor to the symbol.

A couple of things here.  The cursor behavior in EESchema need to copy that
of PCBNew.  If I have both windows open and run a search in EESchema,
PCBNew actually behaves as you would expect it and pans and zooms on the
desired footprint and highlights it even before the Find button is pressed.
Second, Find pop-up dialog should never cover the results of the search.
It is a good feature to remember its last position, but the default
position should be somewhere else, rather than the center of the screen.
Better yet forget Win 3.11 style search and have a simple text box in the
the GUI panel along with the rest of the buttons and add an options drop
down list where you can tune parameters for your search.
```

title: Paste-only pads do not adhere to paste shrinkage (lp:#1837808)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1837808) created by **Evan Shultz (evan-shultz)**
```
I believe some time ago pads with only a paste layer were changed so that
they weren't affected by any paste shrinkage at the footprint level. I have
a vague memory of that on the dev mailing list but I can't find it now.

Anyway, I'm not convinced that this is always the desired behavior.

See https://www.infineon.com/cms/en/product/packages/PG-TISON/PG-
TISON-8-2/. On this footprint there are paste pads for each outer copper
pad which are derived from the outer copper pads with a -0.05mm paste
clearance. That clearance value can be put on the footprint to affect pins
1 and 5 through 8. But on the big copper shape for pins 2-4, there are also
paste pads. It may be fine to place paste-only pads the same size as the
outer copper pads and let them shrink with the footprint paste clearance
instead of making paste-only pads ignore the footprint paste clearance.

I can see paste-only pads adhering to the footprint paste clearance or not
being valuable. And both dialogs where paste clearance can be adjusted have
warning about this, which is nice.

My suggestion is to give flexibility to this behavior, perhaps by adding a
preference option, because in some cases the current behavior isn't the
easiest to use and most intuitive.

See the example footprint I'll add to the next comment. Here the footprint
has one copper pad at the top left, and two paste-only pads on the right.
The footprint has a negative paste clearance, but the paste-only pads don't
shrink at all. If an option to have paste-only pads use the footprint paste
clearance was added, then I would expect the right two pads to shrink.

Note that this applies to mask-only pads as well.
```

title: Assign net classes in pad context menu (lp:#1837636)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1837636) created by **Will Carroll (will.carroll7)**
```
The current procedure for assigning net classes to nets in Pcbnew is
tedious and time-consuming. In order to assign a net class one must open
the "Setup > Design Rules..." dialog and manually sort through the list of
nets to find the desired net, then use the ">>>" net class assignment
widget to assign the net to a net class. Additionally, the Design Rules
dialog disallows any interaction with the editor window while it is open --
requiring the user to repeatedly open and close the dialog.

I propose an enhancement by adding an option to the context menu of a pad
that allows the user to change the net class of the pad's associated net
either through a sub-menu of the new context menu option or through an
additional dialog activated by the new context menu option.


Related:
https://bugs.launchpad.net/kicad/+bug/1787220
This feature request discusses adding a net class reassignment option to
the context menu for a track or via, which was determined in that request
to be the wrong approach, as nets are not associated with tracks and vias,
but with pads.

https://bugs.launchpad.net/kicad/+bug/1749474
This feature request discusses improving the overall design language of
KiCad "to pass engineering notes from the schematic to the layout program".
This would probably involve a way to assign some type of net class
information within Eeschema. Because the only current way to assign net
classes is within Pcbnew through the Design Rules dialog, making this
process faster by adding it to the pad context menu seems logical.

https://bugs.launchpad.net/kicad/+bug/1822493:
This feature request discusses simplifying the net class assignment dialog
so that assigning net classes in bulk via the dialog is easier. It differs
from this request in that this request is proposing a method of reassigning
net classes without having to use the Design Rules dialog.
```

title: Junction added after deletion: end point on wire not "joined" (lp:#1837398)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1837398) created by **Brian Piccioni (br0an)**
```
This just popped up and is 100% repeatable. If I move this block (I've
reduced the schematic to a 4 wires) a junction gets added on SDA and SCL.
It seems that there once were end points where the junctions show up.

If I delete the junctions, they are gone until I move the block then re-
appear as the end points are still there.

I only noticed the extra junctions by accident well after I had completed
the design and started layout after I made a cosmetic change to the board
by shifting the schematic a few mm. I would not normally have run error
checks after such a small change.

I think proper behavior would be for the mid wire end-points to be removed
when the junction is removed so junctions do not automatically re-appear at
a later date.

I can re-create the issue by making 4 wires cross, adding 4 junctions,
deleting 2 junctions, and moving the block.
```

title: Footprint editor - Solder paste ratio clearance issues (lp:#1837220)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1837220) created by **Art (diametrix)**
```
I was trying to enter solder paste clearance issues manually and was
getting puzzling results.  Definitely not the value I entered until I
realized that default value of ratio clearance wasn't zero.   So both of
those values were driving the actual clearance.  You need to zero out one
if another one is manually changed.

BTW,you are using ratio for clearance as a negative value.  By definition,
ratio can't be negative.  Its that pesky math thing.
```

title: pcbnew and footprint editor: export selection as dxf (lp:#1836231)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1836231) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Introduction:
-The 2d drawing capabilities in kicad for lines are limited and creating
complex shapes is easier using a different 2D CAD (librecad, autocad
etc...) to create a dxf file and then import it in pcbnew or footprint
editor with file->import->graphics.
-A whole layer in pcbnew can be exported in dxf format using plot and
choosing dxf format, but this option is not available in the footprint
editor.


Wish:
It should be useful being able to select a group of 2D lines (as a board
outline or a component silk screen etc) and export just the selection
without the need to export the whole layer.

Typical usage case:
Create a 2D shape in an external CAD
Import in kicad
Modify it in kicad
At the change number 12345 you figure out that the next step would be much
easier using the librecad tool "xyz", but editing the original dxf file
implies re-doing the 12344 changes you made in kicad.
so [new feature]: Export the outline you need to change in dxf format
modify it in librecad (or autocad or any..cad)
re-import in kicad.


At least this wishlist can be reduced to "add dxf export or dxf plot to
footprint editor" (probably it would be easier/faster to implement)

Cheers,
Dino.
```

```
Kicad uses the IPC convention of assigning diode cathodes as pin 1 and
anode as pin 2, while the spice simulation engine uses pin 1 as anode.
Although spice models are not included in (most of?) the kicad built-in
libraries, the system appears to recognize diodes and generate a default
spice diode element. The difference in the spice and kicad/IPC conventions
results in incorrect simulations without warning to the user. Additionally,
at no point during use is the user warned that the common diode symbols are
incompatible with the spice simulation feature.

While this is not strictly a bug in the software or mistake in the library,
the two combined results in a significant failure during actual use of the
spice simulation feature.
```

title: Cross ref in schematic text (lp:#1835921)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1835921) created by **Hildo Guillardi Júnior (hildogjr)**
```
Seeing that KiCad is having a effort to update the text box behavior /
features, I propose a new one.
By some code as `\ref{ID_PART1}` the text will create a cross reference
(maybe in the future also hyperlink in the PDF centralizing the referenced
part) that will appear in the text as the reference of the part.

For example, the parts:
R1 -> ID_PART1
R2 -> ID_PART2
R3 -> ID_PART3

In the text:
`\ref{ID_PART1}` became 'R1'
`\ref{ID_PART1, ID_PART3}` became 'R1, R3'
`\ref{ID_PART1, ID_PART2, ID_PART3}` became 'R1-R2'

This will help to do documentations in the project that always have the
correct reference (example: "assemble \ref{ID_PART1} in case of..." will
never refer to a wrong component, if the parts are re-annotated).

To create a good user experience, the text input dialog (in Eeschema and
Pcbnew) could have a button "Add ref" that opens a list of components or
allow click in one to take the UNIQUE ID / TIME STAMP.

Also: the text boxes should be be update in Eschema always that the
"Annotate Schematic" run and in Pcbnew always that sync with Eschema. In
case of not present the ID anymore, the text could be "REF ERRO!".
```

```
Recently, eeschema has been spontaneously crashing very frequently.
Yesterday it crashed for me perhaps two dozen times.  I've not reported it
because I couldn't reproduce it. However, I found a reproducible case this
morning, using the current nightly.

What you see in the linked video
(https://drive.google.com/open?id=15YeV1E9CO4MgU8pfzFPE8cPrTKNE06Ce) is me
beginning a net-highlight operation, then deciding instead to do a place-

net-highlight button again, but eeschema (and kicad as well) crash.  This
seems to happen almost every time I try that particular combination of
operations, but there are other combinations (which I can't presently
identify) that have the same effect.

on in the video:
https://drive.google.com/open?id=10DCzQk6ShE6tyR7gv_M57SUXi1Ty3JEP.  The
video is of the top-level sheet, module.sch.  It may or may not be relevant
that this schematic has a bitmap image in the background template, which
I'm using to position objects during placement.  Another perhaps-novel
feature is that the sheet itself also has a small bitmap image (a logo)
that's not visible in the video.
```

description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1835606) created by **Piotr Gałka (piotrgalka)**
```
Rather wish then bug.
Learning to use KiCad 5.1.2 I found that if:
- I set Highligh collisions Mode,
- I set Mouse drag behaviour to Interactive drag,
then when I put via anywhere where it gets GND net (not important exactly
the net) and then when click that via with mouse (selecting it) and then
grab it to place at another position then colisions highlights. Super - I
didn't found it yesterday even I was searching for such behaviour.

But. When I do the same with any element then its colisions are not
highlighted.
Also if Shove mode is selected and mouse to Interactive drag then dragging
via or element don't activate shoving.

I was thinking about element unconnected yet, but I understand that
elements like to be connected complicating the dragging of them and makeing
it a big work to be done.

But why not make dragging of unconnected elements first (dragging in sense
that colisions are highlighted or tracks pushed) - it would help to
position next set of elements as close as possible to already done part of
PCB.

I think that collisions could be highlighted always when they take place -
even for Move (not Drag) function.
```

title: Current nightly build sometimes does not respect symbol-library pin line-width (lp:#1835051)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1835051) created by **Ron Burkey (rburkey)**
```
In the current nightly build, in a schematic I had created a few days
before, symbol pins all now display with a very tiny line-width.  (See
attached screenshot.)  If I add new symbols, they also have very tiny pin
line-widths.  I checked the symbol library, and there they all displayed
with their previous, normal widths.

In the schematic itself, I used the new Edit Text & Graphics Properties
feature to change all the widths, and the pins then displayed normally.  In
```

description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1834111) created by **Dan Green (danngreen)**
```
Here's how I can reproduce this on OSX. It does it on every project I
tried, for example try the flat_hierarchy demo board.

1. Click on any text item to select it. (If it's a footprint value or
reference, then the blue line to the center of the footprint will be
visible).

2. Click on it again as if you were about to drag it to move it, but do not
move the mouse. Just click on it and keep holding the mouse button down.
Make sure you click off-center.

3. While still holding the mouse button down and making sure you didn't
move the mouse, press the 'm' key (Move hotkey). If you accidentally move
the mouse, the cursor position will jump to the text item center (or vice-
versa) and the bug won't appear.

after that PCBNew will crash. In the latest nightly, it will pop up the
```

title: Option to prevent selecting a footprint on empty area (lp:#1832986)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1832986) created by **eelik (eelik)**
```
I often use large footprints which overlap other footprints. Examples are
"motherboards" as footprints when designing "shields" and OLED displays
with pin header connections where components can be placed under the
display.

It's clumsy that I can often select such a footprint by accident. Zooming
in helps sometimes but not always. I would like to have an option (possibly
file format change?) for such footprints which would prevent selecting them
on the empty area inside the bounding box. They could be selected only by
clicking directly on an item of the footprint (pad, graphic lines etc.).
This should include selecting with box selection - only if an item of the
footprint touches the box, the footprint would be selected.

When Edge.Cuts is enabled for footprints this would also make possible
having outlines as footprints. Otherwise accidentally selecting those
footprints will make using them impractical.
```

title: pcbnew: Clarify DXF Options tooltips (lp:#1832595)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1832595) created by **Olivier (oc-spam66)**
```
Hello,

When I output a DXF file from the "Edge.Cuts" layer, the lines produced are
the inner and outer edges of the KiCad line (taking into account the
linewidth). For an edge of the board, two lines are produced in the DXF
instead of one... and none of them is the real edge of the board! Indeed
manufacturers usually consider that the edge of the board is the center
line (linewidth is not a relevant parameter).

Request: The DXF output of "Edge.Cuts" should be made with single lines,
indicating the real edge of the board (i.e. the center line).

Example of use case: One may want to import the DXF produced by KiCad in a
mechanical CAD software, in order to represent the board edge. In the
current situation, it is painful to remove the duplicate lines and correct
for all the shifted positions.

If it is necessary for someone to have the thickness of the line taken into
account in the DXF, a checkbox could give the user the choice of the type
of line to be drawn in the DXF (either one center line, or two external
lines).

Olivier (KiCad 5.1.2)
```

description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1832081) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Looking around for a possible (easy) implementation for  Bug #1830409
(whishlist) I found that

The labels over and under the child sheet block in a hierarchical schematic
are not always the same.
On screen and in printed version there is the "Sheet: " and "File: " string
prepended, in the plotted version there is not.
Since I don't know if this is intended or not, I report this as a (small)
bug.

This comes from the fact that the string put over the child sheet box in
the schematic is generated differently in different points of the program:

for the on screen string:
sch_painter.cpp line 1299 :        auto text = wxT( "Sheet: " ) +
aSheet->GetName();

For something else (i did not find where this is used, but I'm not very
expert on this source code)
sch_sheet.cpp line 458  :    Text = wxT( "Sheet: " ) + m_name;

for the "print"
sch_sheet.cpp line 484:    wxString text    = wxT( "Sheet: " ) + m_name;

for the "plot" version there is no "Sheet: " string prepended to sheet
name, so I did not find it using a simple "grep Sheet\: *.cpp" (yet).

P.S.: Putting all of that in a single point of the source code may be
better (no more risk of misalignment if/when the string will change or in
translation).

Cheers.
```

title: Add infix (shortcut trigger action) option (lp:#1832011)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1832011) created by **Julien Faucher (suzizecat)**
```
Hi all,

In latest nigthlies, due to eeschema tool framework rework, most of
shortcuts require a mouse click before or after hitting the shortcut key in
order to be triggered.

In example, to move a component, you have to select it and then hit "M".
Another, to draw a wire, hit "W" and then the first click will start the
wire.

It wasn't the case on pre-5.1 versions (at least) and, in my opinion,
working with KiCAD was way faster due to this feature.

However, since this seems to be a battle topic between users/dev I would
suggest the following :
Add an "Use Infix mode" option (infix comes from Cadence Virtuoso, I don't
really care about the actual name)

This would make all tools triggered upon shortcut use, at the mouse pointer
position. Just how it was done in former KiCAD versions. A key modifier (or
even better, a new set of shortcut) could be used to have a reverted-infix
(use infix in normal mode, use tool trigger in infix mode) shortcut.

I really wish to emphasize on the point that not having this behavior
affect deeply the user experience (IMHO in a pretty bad way, but some won't
agree with me on that).

Finally, this might be extended to PCBNew, in order to have a unified
experience.

Best regards,
Julien FAUCHER
```

title: Pcbnew : Custom text font (lp:#1831898)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1831898) created by **Timothée Manaud (timothee)**
```
I̲s̲s̲u̲e̲:̲
When adding text (silk, copper, mask, etc..) there is only one available
font: the default engraving font (IMHO, not really a nice one).

R̲a̲t̲i̲o̲n̲a̲l̲e̲:̲
Because KiCad is getting known from more and more tinkerer, doing trinkets
without enclosure (the product is the bare PCB itself), it would be nice to
have custom font available to improve the final finish of the PCB, with
fancy labels and custom texts on the silk screen.

W̲i̲s̲h̲e̲d̲ ̲f̲e̲a̲t̲u̲r̲e̲:̲
An option to select any system font for text, on any layer, and correct
plotting feature.

W̲o̲r̲k̲a̲r̲o̲u̲n̲d̲:̲ ̲
create a PNG file (eg from Inkscape) with some text with your custom font,
then convert it to a footprint with the bitmap to component converter, edit
the resulting footprint to select the correct layer with a text editor,
then import footprint (or add it to a empty component to the Eeschema or it
will be removed at the text import).
But this is not acceptable as it requires lot of steps, and is not easily
resizable and the layer cannot be selected.

note: the V6 roadmap announce custom font for Eeschema only.
ps: I've not found related issue, please feel free to link to duplicate or
triage to whitelist
```

```
after the import.

user asks for a precise linewidth, he should obtain what he asked for.

In the same manner, the placement translation should be applied after the
scaling. The user want to place the origin of the DXF in the KiCad space.

Olivier (KiCad 5.1.2)
```

title: Common python+Cpp API access pcb and eschamtic file? (lp:#1831166)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1831166) created by **NhatKhai (nhatkhai)**
```
I think it would be great if we have a well define API from Cpp, and can be
access from python to read, write import objects in pcbnew, and eschematic.

This allow:
* Others can develop separate code to convert/translate to difference file
format for ECAD simulation
* Whatever file format Kicad change in future do not effect and external
code
* Event main KiCad itself should use this API. So any new file format do
not impact the code already work.
* New file formats may be access naively when some one can implement to
support current API interface.
* Someone can create a converter from netlist to schematic. Or a simulator
result mode to schematic model.

Importance object mostly to allow to do simulation on schematic level or
pcb level.
```

title: Button/hotkey to recompute net on tracks and vias (lp:#1831046)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1831046) created by **Simon Richter (sjr)**
```
As an easier workflow to reassign a trace from one net to another, it would
be nice if there was a button to recompute the net of tracks and vias from
the connected pads.

This would allow the user to disable DRC, connect the track to a different
pad, recompute nets and reenable DRC, while currently they would have to
disconnect the track, change the net assignment for the next and all
connected segments (which is difficult because many of the nets have long
names computed from the numbers of connected pads), and then connect the
track to the other pad.
```

title: Enable individual symbols and footprints in library tables (lp:#1830946)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1830946) created by **Seppe Stas (seppestas)**
```
This is a feature request / request for comments

I think it would be nice to have some sort of "filter" option for entries
in a library table, especially for symbol libraries. Some use-cases:

- When using some else's libraries you can only have symbols and footprints
that you have already double checked show up by default (my primary use-
case)
- Find symbols that are already used in a project easier / faster
- Reduce the time needed to load libraries

To elaborate on my use-case:

In the company I work for we maintain our own KiCad library with symbols
and footprints. These symbols and footprints where often made by ourselves,
but sometimes symbols and footprints where copied from third party
libraries like the KiCad official libraries. This kind of sucked, since it
was often not clear where the symbols came from, what changes where made to
it and if changes where made they could not easily be contributed back.

We are now trying a new system where we add third-party libraries as git
submodules in our library, however we stumbled upon one limitation we
didn't have when working just copying symbols: we can no longer just select
specific symbols from the third party library. This is important, since we
often found mistakes / quality issues in third party libraries (and even
though the quality of the official libraries improved a lot, we still can't
trust it blindly).

For footprint libraries it is possible to symlink specific specific
footprints into an "in-between" library but this is a bit tedious to
maintain.

For symbol libraries, we came up with a "SYMBOLS" field in the library
table options field. This SYMBOLS filed contains a space separated list of
symbols in the library that have been "double checked" and used in some
project. This way when we start a new project, we can use the symbols in
the "SYMBOLS" list as if we made them ourselves and we now we have to be a
bit more careful with third-party symbols not in this list.

Having a little checkbox to "enable" a symbol in the symbol library browser
that automatically maintains this list would make this approach a lot more
convenient. The same approach could be applied to footprint libraries. When
placing a symbol / selecting a footprint an option could shown to only show
/ load filtered symbols / footprints.

If it's OK I plan to implement this soon and send a patch to the developer
mailing list. I looked into developing it as a plugin, but it's not really
possible to hook in on the symbol selection dialog as far as I can see.

To reduce impact on the library table format I think the "Options" field
could be used, but having a dedicated field might be nicer. Having a
newline separated list would make it nicer to keep track of changes in git
however, i.e a simple git blame could show when a symbol was added to the
list.
```

title: Adding a new library to the global library table will happily use KIPRJMOD by default (lp:#1830694)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1830694) created by **Rene Poeschl (poeschlr)**
```
Adding a library to the library table automatically replaces the file
system path with path variables if possible. This is generally a good
thing. But the use of KIPRJMOD in a global library table will most likely
be a mistake by the user. Meaning simply using it without asking any
questions might not be the best idea.

Example: The user makes a new library using the library editor. It by
default points the user to the location of the project. New users might
simply create the library that way and select "global" in the next dialog
(as they do not know what global/local means). KiCad will then use KIPRJMOD
in the path without the user ever being aware that they might want to
change this. (Which will lead to an error message when opening a different
project.)

There are two options from this point. Adding a project local library to a
global library table could print a warning message that this is not
considered a good idea or kicad could use the full path instead of path
variables. (I lean towards the former as the most likely case here is a
misunderstanding of kicads library system.)
```

title: eeschema hierarchical sheet copy-paste looses child sheet content (lp:#1830633)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1830633) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
Using copy-paste on a child sheet block to have two sheets coming from the
same file creates an empty sheet, possibly loosing data.

To reproduce the bug:

1 Create a project
2 Create a new hierarchical sheet (using "Add a hierarchical sheet").
2.5 Put something inside it (components, connections, etc.)
3 Go back to the parent sheet.
4 use copy-paste to create a new hierarchical sheet. It has the same file
reference (correct)
5 if you enter the new created sheet it is empty (not correct, it should be
the same as the copied sheet).
  if you save the schematic now you loose the old child sheet content. It
seems it is overwritten by the new empty one having the same filename.

6: Workaround: If you edit the properties of the new block in the parent
sheet (shortcut E or right-click->properties), do not change anything and
confirm: a dialog asks for confirm, then the child sheet loads the correct
schematic in it.

Quicker (more dangerous) way to reproduce the bug:
-Open a schematic (that has a backup somewhere) with some hierarchical sub-
sheet
-copy-paste one of them
-save-->...data lost.
```

title: bus members with the same name are merged (lp:#1830233)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1830233) created by **Dino Ghilardi (dino-ghilardi)**
```
If two different buses have members with the same name they are connected
together even if in the schematic there is no connection.

To reproduce the behaviour:
-create two buses using tools->bus definitions, with buses having some
members with the same name
-draw the two buses on the schematic, adding a label over the buses with
the name of the bus
-unfold the members that have the same name
-use "highlight wires and pins of a net" to see that they are connected.
-Also in the netlist passed to pcbnew they will be connected.

...as a workaround we could use different names for every bus member, but
this solution is not optimal (and has drawbacks too).

One possible solution should be using a bus member naming convention for
the bus member like
BUS_NAME[n] (with n numeric) for the buses like address bus A[0] A[1] etc..
BUS_NAME[member_name] for the named members,
but (of course) may be a better approach.
```

title: Eagle import: milling layer is converted to edge cuts layer (lp:#1829708)
description:
[Original report](https://bugs.launchpad.net/bugs/1829708) created by **Rene Poeschl (poeschlr)**
```
The milling layer defines where the milling tool should remove material.
(The centerline defines the toolpath and the width defines the diameter of
the cutter)

The center of lines on the edgecuts layer in kicad (as far as i understand
it) defines the resulting nominal border of the board. (The cutter is
offset from it by half its diameter)

Right now kicad converts lines on the milling layer directly to edge cuts
lines. If my interpretation of the edge cuts layer is correct then the
lines should be converted to two lines and arcs at the end such that the
cutout is defined properly. Or a new layer must be introduced that does the
same as the milling layer in eagle.

Edit: If the edge cuts layer can double as the milling layer (if my
understanding of it is incorrect) then the line width of features on the
milling layer would need to be used for resulting features on the edge cuts
layer. (Right now the edge cuts lines get the default width)
```
